claims.statement: EU food-information law requires listed allergens to be declared and requires upstream businesses supplying non-final food to pass enough information onward for downstream compliance.
EU food businesses must maintain traceability procedures and withdraw unsafe food, creating a durable need for controlled change records.
The Commission's food-safety-management notice treats allergen control as a food-safety-management requirement, but qualified operators remain responsible for HACCP and release decisions.
The reachable sector is large but fragmented: Eurostat reports 4.7 million EU food-and-beverage-processing workers and EUR266 billion of value added in 2022.
Incumbents already advertise supplier portals, version control, BOM linkage, allergen propagation and recipe-to-label impact analysis, so a generic specification repository is not differentiated.

A viable wedge is therefore an integration-first SME exception-clearing service distributed by ingredient distributors or auditors, not a replacement PLM; channel willingness and paid demand remain unverified.

contrary_evidence: TraceGains, Specright, FoodChain ID and Foods Connected publicly offer most core graph, change-control and allergen-impact functions.
The public RASFF interface omits commercial identities, limiting its value for supplier-level incident linkage.
No public evidence establishes distributor feed rights, channel economics or SME willingness to pay per cleared change.

economics.acquisition_route: Seek one regional ingredient distributor as the sole initial anchor customer and permissioned data source through a bounded pilot covering a limited manufacturer cohort; do not assume a distributor commitment, feed right, or separate manufacturer acquisition.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: The former 300-site subscription projection is removed. No defensible path to more than 5 million PLN can yet be quantified from current evidence. The conservative sequence is a paid permissioned anchor pilot, measured positive contribution after review and connector costs, distributor renewal and portfolio expansion, and then replication across additional distributors while retaining founder ownership; timing and value remain unknown until those milestones produce observed contract and margin data.
economics.founder_time: Limit founder work to about 3 hours daily for parsing, connector logic, exception operations and one anchor relationship; qualified customer personnel or a contracted food-safety professional must retain exception review and release authority.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unknown until a scoped distributor pilot measures documents and changes per account, exception rate, human-review time, connector maintenance, support, security and insurance; the prior unsupported 65-75% planning range is not carried forward.
economics.payback: Do not expand beyond the anchor unless measured first-year gross profit after human review, connector, support, security and insurance costs exceeds acquisition and onboarding cost; payback is currently unknown.
economics.pricing: Replace separate onboarding, site-month and per-report manufacturer prices with a distributor-paid managed-service contract whose fee would be set only after a scoped pilot measures covered accounts, change volume, service level and review burden; no price or commitment is asserted.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Renewal and portfolio expansion would depend on the distributor adopting the permissioned change intake and audit trail across supplier and customer accounts; recurrence is plausible from specification changes, but adoption and renewal are unverified.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A contractually permissioned distributor-level corpus of normalized supplier changes, human exception decisions and remediation outcomes improves prioritisation within that distributor's covered portfolio without repurposing confidential formulas
fingerprint.customer: Regional EU ingredient distributors serving small and mid-sized food manufacturers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: A direct anchor sale to an ingredient distributor, followed by deployment inside its supplier and manufacturer account workflow rather than separate SME acquisition
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Distributor-funded managed supplier-change intake, dependency impact triage and human-governed exception service bundled into the distributor's customer service
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The ingredient distributor pays for contracted portfolio coverage and renews or expands coverage after measured service use; manufacturers do not pay separately
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An ingredient supplier changes composition, process, allergen declaration, origin or specification version

founder_fit: Document parsing, dependency modelling, connector logic and exception scoring fit the founder's data-science and AI leverage.

One anchor relationship and no separate SME subscription sales reduce ongoing acquisition load and can fit the founder's part-time limit, although winning and serving a distributor remains an unvalidated enterprise-sales burden.

The founder must not take food-safety release authority; qualified customer personnel or a contracted professional must govern exceptions and releases, adding cost and coordination that the pilot must measure.

redesign.economic_effect: Replaces a 300-site manufacturer subscription model and unpriced channel share with one distributor as payer, permissioned feed source and deployment channel. The conservative path now advances only from a paid scoped anchor pilot to renewal, portfolio expansion and multi-distributor replication when observed contract revenue exceeds measured human-review, connector, support, security, insurance, acquisition and onboarding costs; no price, margin, commitment or wealth timing is assumed.

risks: A missed allergen dependency could harm consumers; the service must never auto-release labels and requires immutable audit trails, access controls and qualified human review.
Dependence on one anchor creates concentration, bargaining and termination risk, while incumbent PLM vendors can bundle the workflow or block integrations.

Supplier specifications and formulas are commercially sensitive; a distributor contract must grant narrowly scoped processing, feed and derived-data rights, and no such rights are currently established.
The distributor may not accept liability, fund the service or persuade manufacturers to use it, and human review, security and insurance may prevent positive contribution.

structure.control_point: The distributor's permissioned supplier-change intake and human-approved exception trail across covered manufacturer accounts
structure.critical_dependency: A distributor anchor willing to pay and grant timely, narrowly scoped feed and processing rights, plus qualified human exception and release ownership

thesis: Sell a permissioned supplier-change intake and human-governed exception service to a regional ingredient distributor as the anchor payer and data source, bundling it into covered manufacturer accounts instead of charging SMEs separately, while qualified personnel retain every label and release decision.
title: Distributor Supplier-Change Desk
uncertainties: Whether an ingredient distributor will pay, provide timely feeds and grant narrowly scoped processing and derived-data rights without an assumed commitment.
Whether covered account count, change volume and contract value can support positive contribution after human review, connector, support, security and insurance costs.
Whether manufacturer users will adopt the distributor-bundled workflow and qualified personnel will accept its audit trail rather than existing PLM, portals or spreadsheets.
Achievable extraction and exception accuracy, onboarding effort and review burden across languages and inconsistent supplier formats.
Renewal, portfolio expansion and replication across distributors are unvalidated, leaving the founder-wealth path and timing unquantified.
